title: Evaporation
text: I am currently lying in wait on the Melromarc Plains, the site of the decisive battle. The Dragon King, which ravaged Melromarc, has been rounded up by Filolial-sama and his companions. A raincloud—so vast it obscures the sky—pouring down a torrent of strong acid is closing in, chasing after Filolial-sama and his group. I don’t think defeating it will be difficult in and of itself.
However, the problem is the time limit we have to defeat it. There’s still a little time left before our meeting with my Father and the others. If we let the battle drag on, we won’t make it in time.
That said, we can’t act too soon either. We must do our best to stay vigilant and minimize casualties as much as possible.
“It’s nearly time to fight. Today, we will finally defeat the Four Spirits that have caused so much destruction and bring peace to the world.”

The soldiers of Melromarc raise their weapons in response to my voice. They’re casting their strongest magical shields to withstand the rain of strong acid. I’ll take the lead, and the soldiers of the Melromarc Army will focus on providing support.
Well, I can’t really expect them to be all that strong, after all. Now, all that’s left is to wait for Filolial-sama to arrive.
With a thunderous roar and a cloud of sand, Filolial-sama and her companions guided the Dragon King toward me.
“Everyone, you’ve done a great job! Now, I’d like you all to take up positions in the rear and provide support with Magic.”
“‘Yes, ma’am!’”

With a spirited, perfectly synchronized reply and a single wing raised to signal me, Filolial-sama and the others formed a formation to protect the Melromarc Army. Then, under the command of the Queen who leads the Melromarc Army, they began chanting Ceremonial Magic and support Magic.

The Dragon Kings, gathered in one spot, coalesced into a single massive cloud, revealing a silhouette reminiscent of an Eastern dragon through the clouds. Since they are the Four Spirits, their forms are unstable. Most likely, their shape will shift and change just as it did during our last battle. With only a little time left until the moment I agreed upon with Father, I’ll focus on weakening them until just before I deliver the finishing blow.
“Al Liberation Prominence!”

Just as before, I create a pseudo-sun to blast away the rain clouds and fire it upward. Then, to block the rain clouds’ escape route, Filolial-sama and the others use wind magic to manipulate the atmosphere.
The Dragon King has emerged from the rain clouds. It takes the form of a classic Eastern dragon.
“Brionac X!”

As I fired Brionac straight at its head, the Dragon King countered by unleashing a breath attack. It was a breath containing water and lightning, like a torrential flood. It crackled and seemed powerful enough to hold its own against my Brionac.

However, little by little, my Brionac is gaining the upper hand. Just as Father said, the Four Spirits—having pooled their strength—are displaying their power in plain sight. Well, it doesn’t seem strong enough to deflect my enhanced Brionac, though.
“Gungnir X!”

This is a continuous attack where I unleash Gungnir while firing my Brionac. Well, since I have two hands, something like this is possible. No, if I master it, I should be able to launch the Aiming Lancer at the same time.

I should be able to do it by launching the spear from the Float Lance, using the same technique my Father used with the Floating Shield. There’s no problem as long as you use a different skill during the cooldown. Anyway, it’s been a while since I’ve faced a challenging opponent—I’ll make sure to take it down by the time Father specified!

My All Cannon Fire sent the Dragon King’s body flying off into thin air. However, it seems far from a fatal blow. The Dragon King, which had been flying through the sky, fell to the ground and melted into the earth, causing multiple heads to appear.

This form bears a striking resemblance to the combat form Takt’s dragon used to take. And now, each of the multiple heads is preparing to unleash multiple breath attacks. Their targets are clearly me, Filolial-sama behind me, and the Melromarc Army.
“I won’t let you! Meteor Thrust X! Aiming Lancer X!”
I’ll take out every single head before they can unleash their breath attacks!

The Dragon King seems to be letting out a cry of utter shock, unable even to counterattack. But even this cry possesses offensive power. For ordinary people, this sonic attack would be far more than just painful. The area is vibrating with a tingling sensation.
“Amazing… That must be the legendary Spear Hero…”
“But those Four Spirits of Calamity, who are withstanding the attacks of the Spear Hero, are monsters in their own right.”

I can hear voices of astonishment coming from the Melromarc army. This is a piece of cake for me. What we need to watch out for is the Silence Breath. If you get hit by that, healing will be a hassle.

After all, that breath has a wide range. It flashes, and the moment you’re hit by that light, the Silence effect kicks in. Moreover, to silence even me or my Father, the Melromarc soldiers would need some pretty high-level potions or Magic. If that happens, I’ll have to focus my mind to cast a healing spell.

Back then, it was just a fragment of the Dragon King, so I had some leeway, but this is a collective of Dragon Kings gathered from all over Melromarc. I doubt I’ll have time to leisurely cast healing magic.

I’ve cast a preventive spell in advance… but since my specialties are fire and healing magic, this is slightly outside my area of expertise. Situations like this also require support magic, so my Father would be the best person to handle prevention. However, he’s not here—he’s fighting the Qilin.
“We’re not done yet!　Air Strike Javelin! Second Javelin! Drill Javelin!”

I’ll keep attacking the Dragon King in rapid succession with my basic Skills. After all, the Dragon King is a tough opponent. It’s like fighting living water, so it’s going to be a struggle to finish it off.

Another roar. I’ll check the damage situation in the rear. For the most part, Filolial-sama and the others are safe, but it looks like some members of the Melromarc Army have sustained minor damage. Since the cooldown has ended, I unleash Brionac and Gungnir once more.

But… it really is tough. It looks like it’s gradually shrinking in size—could that be proof that my attacks are having an effect? To deliver the finishing blow, Magic would likely be most effective. After all, that’s how we defeated it last time… or so it seems.

But for now, let’s prioritize holding the Dragon King back as much as possible and defeating it exactly as planned. I’ll unleash Skills one after another to gradually weaken it. We mustn’t let our guard down. Back in the first world, when we fought the Phoenix, the very moment we thought we had the upper hand, we were thrown into a pinch by Takt’s attack.
“I’ll take care of this!”
And just like that, some guy who looked like an adventurer—for some reason ignoring our plan—dashed forward.
“What’s so great about a ‘Hero’! This is our chance to shine—”

Where on earth did he come from? Ordinary adventurers who have no intention of cooperating with the military should have already been ordered to leave the country. Just then, the Dragon King locked onto its target and unleashed a breath attack.
“Aiming Lancer X!”
I cast Skills to deflect the breath and protect them, but…
“By chance, I landed the finishing blow and earned us a special—”

It was too late; the group of adventurers vaporized. At a glance, it looked like one man and three pigs. What on earth was that about? To charge at the Dragon King while ignoring both orders and warnings… Are they just idiots?
Well, the time my father set is drawing near. From here on out, it’s a race against time, just as planned. We need to quickly defeat the Dragon King before time runs out.

Soon, the time my father specified arrived, and the Melromarc Army in the rear gave the signal. At the same moment, the number 9 floating in my field of vision began to flash. Oh… that’s my father for you. Well then, now it’s my turn.
An illustration of a spear that has completely forgotten the warning it received from the shield.
